description: GUARD BYPASS via title substring. The NUM guard at line 12 treats an article as Automaton if 'Automaton' appears anywhere in the title OR 'automaton' anywhere in NOTE_SRC (case-insensitive). This means a NON-Automaton article whose title merely mentions the word 'automaton' (e.g. an article ABOUT automaton theory, finite automata, or quoting the Automaton project) is classified _is_automaton=True, so the guard at line 12-13 does NOT fire, and the article can be uploaded to NOTE_NUM=166686292 (the real Automaton note) — overwriting the live Automaton article with unrelated content. The guard is a substring heuristic, not an identity check; it conflates 'the article is THE Automaton article (note 166686292)' with 'the article contains the word automaton'. INV-1/INV-2 only test the exact-default and a fully-clean fixture, so this collision is never exercised.

evidence.snippet:
_SRC=os.environ.get("NOTE_SRC",""); _is_automaton=("Automaton" in title) or ("automaton" in _SRC.lower())
if NUM=="166686292" and not _is_automaton: raise SystemExit(...)

fix: Do not infer identity from a content substring. Bind 166686292 to the canonical Automaton SRC path (os.path.realpath(NOTE_SRC) == realpath of the default automaton-jp.md) rather than to the word 'automaton' appearing in title/SRC. Better: require an explicit allow flag/env to write to 166686292 and refuse otherwise, so no content coincidence can target the live note.
